scope: The exact 16-image public-route matrix: the twelve unchanged selection screens retained from the prior review plus four changed initial-gameplay screens reviewed at original resolution. Six additional changed mobile/raw-canvas regression PNGs were also reviewed at original resolution. Narrow approval to record deterministic baselines does not imply visual acceptance.
resolvedFindings: The detached black workshop wall bays are gone; retained wall caps and scenery bases read as deliberate solid architecture.
Enemy health fill is contained inside a connected ornamental frame with no detached red or transparent spill.
The irregular rock floor is visually coherent, and collision-relevant buildings, crates, lanterns, and masonry have legible grounded footprints.
Portrait and landscape touch controls remain contained, reachable, and clear of the central encounter.
rejectedFindings: Ashfang still reads as a prone corpse or collapsed heap rather than a living moving threat.
Wide, landscape, and raw-canvas compositions devote too much of the frame to empty ground and under-stage the encounter.
Mobile microcopy is barely readable at physical play size.
Enemy health bars are overly bright and blocky relative to the restrained environment palette.
Several combat frames overlap the player and Ashfang ambiguously, and faint terrain-block seams remain visible in wide profiles.
Still-image approval cannot establish gait smoothness, support transfer, camera continuity, or the absence of frame-to-frame jumping; temporal evidence remains mandatory.
promotionRule: This 6.7/10 rejection applies only while both the contract and ordered public screenshot-set hashes match. Narrow approval records reviewed regression pixels but cannot promote visual quality. Any pixel or contract change invalidates the rejection and returns the gallery to candidate; no machine metric can override a matching rejection.
